pmf-cdf.text: The PMF gives the probability at a value. The CDF sums probabilities at all values up to a threshold.
pmf-cdf.title: The PMF gives the probability at a value. The CDF sums probabilities at all values up to a threshold.

cdf-interval.text: For any distribution, probability a < X ≤ b equals F(b) minus F(a); probability X > b is one minus F(b).
cdf-interval.title: For any distribution, probability a < X ≤ b equals F(b) minus F(a); probability X > b is one minus F(b).

pmf-valid.text: Masses are nonnegative and sum to one. The CDF stays between zero and one and has limits zero and one.
pmf-valid.title: Masses are nonnegative and sum to one. The CDF stays between zero and one and has limits zero and one.

expected.text: Expectation is the probability-weighted mean. Variance is the probability-weighted squared distance from the mean. Standard deviation is its square root.
expected.title: Expectation is the probability-weighted mean. Variance is the probability-weighted squared distance from the mean. Standard deviation is its square root.

affine.text: A linear transformation changes the mean by a times the mean plus b, variance by a squared, and standard deviation by absolute a.
affine.title: A linear transformation changes the mean by a times the mean plus b, variance by a squared, and standard deviation by absolute a.

second.text: Variance equals the second raw moment minus the square of the mean.
second.title: Variance equals the second raw moment minus the square of the mean.

moment-proof.text: Expand the weighted sum for linearity. Expand the squared deviation for the second-moment identity. Fixed shifts cancel from deviations.
moment-proof.title: Expand the weighted sum for linearity. Expand the squared deviation for the second-moment identity. Fixed shifts cancel from deviations.

joint-formulas.tex: p_{X,Y}(x,y)=P(X=x,Y=y),\quad p_X(x)=\sum_y p_{X,Y}(x,y),\quad F_{X,Y}(a,b)=\sum_{x\le a}\sum_{y\le b}p_{X,Y}(x,y)
joint-formulas.text: The joint PMF gives pair probabilities. Marginalize by summing over the other variable; the joint CDF sums the lower-left rectangle.
joint-formulas.title: The joint PMF gives pair probabilities. Marginalize by summing over the other variable; the joint CDF sums the lower-left rectangle.

covariance.text: Covariance is the expected product of centered variables. Means add without independence; the variance of a weighted sum includes twice the weighted covariance.
covariance.title: Covariance is the expected product of centered variables. Means add without independence; the variance of a weighted sum includes twice the weighted covariance.

sum-proof.text: Expand the square of the centered sum to obtain two variances and twice the covariance.
sum-proof.title: Expand the square of the centered sum to obtain two variances and twice the covariance.

discrete-uniform.text: For a uniform finite set, each value has probability one over the number of values; moments average over the set.
discrete-uniform.title: For a uniform finite set, each value has probability one over the number of values; moments average over the set.

bernoulli.text: Bernoulli has two possible values with mean p and variance p times one minus p.
bernoulli.title: Bernoulli has two possible values with mean p and variance p times one minus p.

binomial.text: The binomial PMF counts the arrangements of x successes in n independent trials with a common p.
binomial.title: The binomial PMF counts the arrangements of x successes in n independent trials with a common p.

poisson.text: Poisson counts nonnegative integers, with a mean and variance equal to lambda.
poisson.title: Poisson counts nonnegative integers, with a mean and variance equal to lambda.

hypergeom.text: Hypergeometric probability chooses x tagged and n−x untagged items from a finite population, within its feasible integer support.
hypergeom.title: Hypergeometric probability chooses x tagged and n−x untagged items from a finite population, within its feasible integer support.

hypergeom-moments.text: Hypergeometric variance is the binomial-like variance times the finite-population correction, for N greater than one.
hypergeom-moments.title: Hypergeometric variance is the binomial-like variance times the finite-population correction, for N greater than one.

binomial-proof.text: The combinatorial identity reduces the binomial first moment. The second factorial moment yields the variance.
binomial-proof.title: The combinatorial identity reduces the binomial first moment. The second factorial moment yields the variance.

poisson-limit.tex: \lim_{n\to\infty}\binom nx\left(\frac\lambda n\right)^x\left(1-\frac\lambda n\right)^{n-x}=\frac{\lambda^x e^{-\lambda}}{x!}\quad(\lambda\text{ and }x\text{ fixed})
poisson-limit.text: Let the number of trials grow with success probability lambda divided by n. For fixed lambda and count, the binomial PMF converges to Poisson.
poisson-limit.title: Let the number of trials grow with success probability lambda divided by n. For fixed lambda and count, the binomial PMF converges to Poisson.

poisson-proof.text: Use the exponential series and shift the count index to obtain the Poisson moments.
poisson-proof.title: Use the exponential series and shift the count index to obtain the Poisson moments.

hypergeom-proof.text: The hypergeometric factorial moment counts ordered pairs of sampled successes; subtracting the squared mean gives the variance.
hypergeom-proof.title: The hypergeometric factorial moment counts ordered pairs of sampled successes; subtracting the squared mean gives the variance.

density-def.text: A density is nonnegative with unit area. Integrate to obtain the CDF; subtract CDF values for interval probabilities.
density-def.title: A density is nonnegative with unit area. Integrate to obtain the CDF; subtract CDF values for interval probabilities.

quantile.tex: q_p=F^{-1}(p),\qquad P(X\le q_p)=p\quad\text{for a continuous strictly increasing CDF}
quantile.text: A quantile turns a target cumulative probability into a threshold value.
quantile.title: A quantile turns a target cumulative probability into a threshold value.

density-derivative.tex: P(x<X\le x+\Delta)\approx f(x)\Delta,\qquad f(x)=F^{\prime}(x)\quad\text{where the derivative exists}
density-derivative.text: A narrow interval has probability approximately density times width. The density is the derivative of the CDF where defined.
density-derivative.title: A narrow interval has probability approximately density times width. The density is the derivative of the CDF where defined.

continuous-moments.text: Continuous moments are weighted integrals rather than weighted sums, when the moments exist.
continuous-moments.title: Continuous moments are weighted integrals rather than weighted sums, when the moments exist.

uniform-pdf-cdf.text: The uniform density is constant between a and b, zero outside. Its CDF is zero below a, linear within, and one above b.
uniform-pdf-cdf.title: The uniform density is constant between a and b, zero outside. Its CDF is zero below a, linear within, and one above b.

uniform-moments.text: Uniform mean, second moment, variance and quantile follow directly from its constant density.
uniform-moments.title: Uniform mean, second moment, variance and quantile follow directly from its constant density.

exponential.text: The exponential model uses rate r, with mean one over r and variance one over r squared. Density and CDF are zero for negative time.
exponential.title: The exponential model uses rate r, with mean one over r and variance one over r squared. Density and CDF are zero for negative time.

memoryless.text: Exponential waiting is memoryless: the probability of waiting t more time after s is the same as the original survival probability for t.
memoryless.title: Exponential waiting is memoryless: the probability of waiting t more time after s is the same as the original survival probability for t.

uniform-proof.text: Integrate x and x squared against a constant density to get uniform moments.
uniform-proof.title: Integrate x and x squared against a constant density to get uniform moments.

exp-proof.text: No arrivals by time t gives exponential survival. Integration by parts yields the first two moments and inverse CDF gives the quantile.
exp-proof.title: No arrivals by time t gives exponential survival. Integration by parts yields the first two moments and inverse CDF gives the quantile.

normal-pdf.text: The normal density is centered at mu and scaled by positive sigma. Subtract the mean and divide by the standard deviation to standardize.
normal-pdf.title: The normal density is centered at mu and scaled by positive sigma. Subtract the mean and divide by the standard deviation to standardize.

normal-tails.text: Standardize each bound before subtracting standard-normal CDF values. Quantiles reverse the process. A right-tail critical value uses one minus alpha.
normal-tails.title: Standardize each bound before subtracting standard-normal CDF values. Quantiles reverse the process. A right-tail critical value uses one minus alpha.

normal-linear.tex: aX+b\sim N(a\mu+b,a^2\sigma^2)\quad(a\ne0);\qquad X\pm Y\sim N(\mu_X\pm\mu_Y,\sigma_X^2+\sigma_Y^2)\quad\text{if independent normal}
normal-linear.text: An affine transform of a normal remains normal when its multiplier is nonzero. Independent normal sums and differences add variances.
normal-linear.title: An affine transform of a normal remains normal when its multiplier is nonzero. Independent normal sums and differences add variances.

gaussian.text: Square the integral, change to polar coordinates with Jacobian r, and evaluate to pi. Taking the positive square root normalizes the Gaussian.
gaussian.title: Square the integral, change to polar coordinates with Jacobian r, and evaluate to pi. Taking the positive square root normalizes the Gaussian.

radial.text: Continuity and positivity turn the multiplicative functional equation into an exponential. Integrability forces a negative coefficient, giving a Gaussian.
radial.title: Continuity and positivity turn the multiplicative functional equation into an exponential. Integrability forces a negative coefficient, giving a Gaussian.

normal-moments.text: Odd symmetry gives standard-normal mean zero. Integration by parts gives second moment one. Location and scale then produce mu and sigma squared.
normal-moments.title: Odd symmetry gives standard-normal mean zero. Integration by parts gives second moment one. Location and scale then produce mu and sigma squared.

normal-shape.text: A normal is symmetric about its mean. Standardized skewness is zero and kurtosis is three, so excess kurtosis is zero.
normal-shape.title: A normal is symmetric about its mean. Standardized skewness is zero and kurtosis is three, so excess kurtosis is zero.

chi-square.text: Sum the squares of independent standard normals to obtain a chi-square distribution with the number of terms as degrees of freedom.
chi-square.title: Sum the squares of independent standard normals to obtain a chi-square distribution with the number of terms as degrees of freedom.

student-t.text: A standard normal divided by the square root of an independent chi-square divided by its degrees of freedom has a Student t distribution.
student-t.title: A standard normal divided by the square root of an independent chi-square divided by its degrees of freedom has a Student t distribution.

f-family.text: Divide two independent chi-square variables by their respective degrees of freedom, then form their ratio to obtain F.
f-family.title: Divide two independent chi-square variables by their respective degrees of freedom, then form their ratio to obtain F.

chi-density.text: The chi-square density uses the gamma function and has support on positive values.
chi-density.title: The chi-square density uses the gamma function and has support on positive values.

t-density.text: Student t density is symmetric and depends on degrees of freedom through gamma normalization and a power tail.
t-density.title: Student t density is symmetric and depends on degrees of freedom through gamma normalization and a power tail.

f-density.text: The F density is a positive-support ratio density with beta-function normalization.
f-density.title: The F density is a positive-support ratio density with beta-function normalization.

poisson-limit-ratio.text: The exact adjacent binomial ratio is (n minus x) over (x plus one), times p over (one minus p). With p equal to lambda over n, it tends to lambda over (x plus one), for fixed lambda and x.
poisson-limit-ratio.title: The exact adjacent binomial ratio is (n minus x) over (x plus one), times p over (one minus p). With p equal to lambda over n, it tends to lambda over (x plus one), for fixed lambda and x.

poisson-limit-zero.text: The probability of zero successes is (one minus lambda over n) to the power n. Its limit is e to the power minus lambda.
poisson-limit-zero.title: The probability of zero successes is (one minus lambda over n) to the power n. Its limit is e to the power minus lambda.

poisson-limit-recurrence.text: Starting at q zero, multiply successively by lambda over one, lambda over two, and lambda over three. At count x the denominators form x factorial, giving e to minus lambda times lambda to x divided by x factorial.
poisson-limit-recurrence.title: Starting at q zero, multiply successively by lambda over one, lambda over two, and lambda over three. At count x the denominators form x factorial, giving e to minus lambda times lambda to x divided by x factorial.

poisson-limit-normalization.text: The limiting masses sum to e to minus lambda times the exponential series for e to lambda, which equals one.
poisson-limit-normalization.title: The limiting masses sum to e to minus lambda times the exponential series for e to lambda, which equals one.
